# FastSearch

> FastSearch is an open-source .NET library for lightning-fast, case-insensitive substring searching across large collections of objects. It provides three search algorithms — CharSequenceSearch (suffix trie), HashSearch (precomputed hashes), and LinqSearch (parallel LINQ). Built by Microsoft MVP Richard Crane at MILL5. Available on NuGet.

- **Name:** FastSearch
- **Version:** 1.0.16

## Algorithms

FastSearch provides three search algorithms, all implementing `ISearch<T>`:

### CharSequenceSearch (Recommended)
Builds a suffix trie at index time from all string representations of your objects. At query time, walks the trie character-by-character for O(k) lookups where k is the search string length. Uses ConcurrentDictionary and Parallel.ForEach for thread-safe, multi-threaded indexing. Ideal for autocomplete, type-ahead, and large datasets.

### HashSearch
Precomputes hash values for every substring during indexing. Delivers constant-time hash lookups at query time. Best for fixed-length search patterns and high-throughput batch scenarios.

### LinqSearch
Uses Parallel LINQ to search collections concurrently at query time. No upfront indexing cost. Good for smaller or frequently-changing collections.

## How it works

1. **Install** FastSearch from NuGet: `dotnet add package FastSearch`
2. **Create** a search instance with your collection: `var search = new CharSequenceSearch<string>(items);`
3. **Search** with any substring: `var results = search.Search("query");` — returns matching items instantly.

FastSearch accepts any `IEnumerable<T>` where T is a class. Items are indexed by their `ToString()` representation, or you can provide a custom `Func<T, string[]>` to specify which strings to index per item.

## Technical details

- **Indexing complexity:** O(N × L²) where N = number of items, L = average string length
- **Search complexity:** O(k × C) where k = search string length, C = average matches per trie node
- **Concurrency model:** ConcurrentDictionary for trie nodes, Parallel.ForEach for indexing, fine-grained locks (Interlocked operations) for node updates
- **Data structure:** Suffix trie with CharSequence nodes containing Character, NextCharacters (ConcurrentDictionary), and Items (HashSet with ReferenceEqualityComparer)
- **Case handling:** All strings lowercased at index time for case-insensitive matching
- **Thread safety:** Indexing is thread-safe via concurrent data structures; queries are inherently thread-safe on the read-only trie

## Use cases

- **Autocomplete / type-ahead search** in web, desktop, or mobile applications
- **Password search / breach checking** against large password lists
- **Name lookup** across employee directories, contact lists, CRM systems
- **Product search** in e-commerce catalogs
- **Log searching** across application log entries
- **Any scenario** requiring fast substring matching over in-memory collections
